# Results — Study 910 (Managed-Distribution CEF)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **persistent-discount
closed-end funds with a big "managed distribution" hand the buyer both the discount pull and the
payout, a structural double-carry the index can't offer** — measured on the buyer's bottom line:
does holding these CEFs deliver a **real excess-of-cash, risk-adjusted return vs the asset class**,
or does NAV erosion / embedded leverage cost collapse it to levered beta (the mREIT lesson of
[611-mreit-carry](../../611-mreit-carry/))? Tested on **PCEF** (the CEF-of-CEFs) and an equal-weight
basket of four large single-name CEFs (**PDI, UTF, BST, RQI**) vs **SPY**, all excess of **BIL**
(cash). yfinance `auto_adjust=True` **total-return** closes — every distribution reinvested, so the
number we hold is the honest economic return whatever label the fund put on the cash. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. Data
as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `cae85d4d2cca`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes: PCEF, PDI, UTF, BST, RQI, SPY, BIL — public, no key |
| Window | 2003-01-02 → 2026-06-30 daily; **281**-row monthly panel; per-fund windows start at each fund's inception (basket 2014-11, PCEF 2010-03) |
| Cash / risk-free leg | **BIL** (SPDR 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF); every Sharpe and mean here is **excess-of-cash** (both legs minus BIL) |
| Basket | equal-weight, monthly-rebalanced **PDI/UTF/BST/RQI**; composition-stable (starts at BST's 2014-10 inception) |
| Inference | **Newey-West HAC *t*** (6 lags) on means and on the excess-vs-excess CAPM `r_ex(fund)=α+β·r_ex(SPY)`; moving-block bootstrap Sharpe CI |
| Costs | CEF bid-ask **15 bps one-way** on the monthly rebalance (~10 %/yr two-sided turnover); leverage cost is **already embedded** in the total return, so no extra borrow is levied |

> **Survivorship / short-history — named on the Signal axis.** These are the *flagship* CEFs that
> gathered assets and survived; funds that blew up on their leverage are absent, so any positive
> read is an **upper bound**. The four-name basket has only ~11.5 years of tape (BST-limited);
> PCEF gives ~16 years for the diversified proxy.

## Per-fund — a real excess-of-cash return, but it TRAILS SPY risk-adjusted

Excess-of-cash (minus BIL), each fund's own full window; `α`/`β` are the excess-vs-excess CAPM
vs SPY. **Sharpe adv** = fund excess-of-cash Sharpe − SPY's on the same months.

| fund | window | n | exret (bps/mo) | HAC *t* | exSharpe | SPY exSharpe | **adv** | α (%/yr) | *t*(α) | β | R² | max DD |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| PCEF | 2010-03→2026-06 | 196 | +49.3 | +2.48 | 0.51 | 0.92 | **−0.41** | −3.3 | −1.96 | 0.69 | 0.75 | −24 % |
| PDI  | 2012-06→2026-06 | 169 | +75.4 | +2.61 | 0.62 | 0.97 | −0.35 | +0.7 | +0.18 | 0.61 | 0.35 | −32 % |
| UTF  | 2007-06→2026-06 | 229 | +76.7 | +1.77 | 0.43 | 0.64 | −0.21 | −0.6 | −0.18 | 0.97 | 0.51 | −62 % |
| BST  | 2014-11→2026-06 | 140 | +138.5 | +2.60 | 0.73 | 0.82 | −0.09 | +1.5 | +0.35 | 1.23 | 0.65 | −45 % |
| RQI  | 2007-06→2026-06 | 229 | +92.8 | +1.31 | 0.31 | 0.64 | −0.34 | −4.7 | −0.81 | 1.57 | 0.46 | **−87 %** |

Every fund earns a **positive excess-of-cash return** — the distributions are *not* pure
return-of-capital capital destruction (that would print a negative total return; here total
returns clear cash, several at HAC *t* > 2). **But the Sharpe advantage vs SPY is negative for
every single fund**, the CAPM alpha is ~0-to-negative (PCEF's −3.3 %/yr is *significantly*
negative at *t* = −1.96), and the betas (0.6–1.6) show the return is asset-class exposure, often
levered. RQI — a leveraged real-estate CEF — is the [611-mreit-carry](../../611-mreit-carry/)
trap in miniature: a **−87 % drawdown** and a −4.7 %/yr alpha.

## The headline — equal-weight basket (PDI/UTF/BST/RQI), monthly rebalanced

| quantity | basket | SPY |
|---|--:|--:|
| window / n | 2014-11 → 2026-06 / 140 mo | same |
| annualised total return | +11.5 % | +13.8 % |
| annualised vol | 17 % | — |
| **excess-of-cash return** | **+88.3 bps/mo (HAC *t* = +2.63)** | — |
| **excess-of-cash Sharpe** | **0.61** | **0.82** |
| **Sharpe advantage** | **−0.21** | — |
| basket − SPY (monthly) | −13.6 bps (*t* = −0.69) | — |
| CAPM α / β / R² | **−1.6 %/yr (*t* = −0.59)** / 1.00 / 0.73 | — |
| max drawdown | −28 % | — |

**Bootstrap Sharpe CI (moving-block, 5,000 resamples):** basket **0.61 [0.12, 1.17]**
(frac_neg = 0.005); PCEF **0.51 [0.08, 1.03]** (frac_neg = 0.007). The excess-of-cash Sharpe is
robustly **positive** — the payout is a real return — but the whole interval sits **below SPY's
0.82**. Net of beta, the basket is a **levered-beta income clone**: β = 1.00 to equities (high
for a supposed "income" sleeve), R² = 0.73, and an alpha indistinguishable from — indeed slightly
below — zero.

## Era cut at 2022-01 — the rate-hike regime broke it

When the Fed hiked, leverage got expensive and CEF discounts blew out. The excess return **halved
to statistical zero** and the alpha turned sharply negative — in *both* the basket and PCEF.

| | window | n | exret (bps/mo) | HAC *t* | exSharpe | SPY | adv | α (%/yr) | *t*(α) | β |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **basket** pre | 2014-11→2021-12 | 86 | +123.9 | +2.94 | 0.90 | 1.00 | −0.10 | +1.2 | +0.32 | 0.96 |
| **basket** post | 2022-01→2026-06 | 54 | +31.6 | +0.62 | 0.20 | 0.56 | −0.36 | −5.5 | −1.62 | 1.04 |
| **PCEF** pre | 2010-03→2021-12 | 142 | +62.0 | +2.82 | 0.69 | 1.08 | −0.39 | −2.3 | −0.98 | 0.65 |
| **PCEF** post | 2022-01→2026-06 | 54 | +16.0 | +0.39 | 0.14 | 0.56 | −0.42 | **−5.0** | **−2.78** | 0.78 |

The Sharpe advantage is **negative in every sub-era**; there is no cut in which the CEF wrapper
risk-adjusted-beats its asset class. Calendar-2022 alone cost the basket **−24.4 %**.

**Calendar-year total returns — basket (%):** 2015 +3.0 · 2016 +12.7 · 2017 +29.8 · 2018 −0.9 ·
2019 +38.8 · 2020 +11.4 · 2021 +20.3 · **2022 −24.4** · 2023 +13.6 · 2024 +17.0 · 2025 +11.6 ·
2026 (H1) +15.9.

## Tradability — costs are NOT the killer; a hidden levered beta is

| version | exret (bps/mo) | HAC *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| gross | +88.3 | +2.63 | 0.61 |
| net (15 bps CEF spread × turnover) | +88.0 | +2.62 | 0.61 |
| SPY (excess-of-cash) | — | — | **0.82** |

Charge is **0.25 bps/mo** — these are buy-and-hold funds, so trading friction barely dents the
number (net ≈ gross). The edge dies not at the trading desk but in the **factor regression**: the
levered equity beta (~1.0, R² 0.73) means you get a **better risk-adjusted return just holding
SPY**, and post-2022 the excess return collapsed to +32 bps (*t* < 1) with a −5.5 %/yr alpha. A
hidden beta — not costs — erases it: **Mirage**, not Fragile.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful *(never market evidence)*

Deterministic world (`synthetic_world`, seed 910): a levered claim on a market factor (β = 1.1)
plus a tunable structural carry and a return-of-capital leak.

| world | recovered α (%/yr) | HAC *t*(α) | β |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (pure levered beta, carry 0) | −1.46 | −0.86 | 1.11 |
| planted +5 %/yr net carry | +3.54 | **+2.10** | 1.11 |
| return-of-capital trap (carry == leak) | −1.46 | −0.86 | 1.11 |

The estimator recovers the planted carry as alpha (the +5 pp lift is exact: −1.46 → +3.54) and
recovers the planted leverage as β ≈ 1.1. The **null does not fire** (|t| = 0.86; over 20 seeds
|t| ≥ 2 in only 2/20 — a clean ~5 % false-positive rate). Crucially the **return-of-capital trap
is indistinguishable from the null**: a fat payout that is 100 % return-of-capital yields **no
alpha** — exactly the mechanism that flattens the real CEFs' advantage. So the real-tape reading
(positive excess-of-cash return, zero-to-negative alpha, negative Sharpe advantage) is the genuine
article, not an artefact.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The payout is *real*: these persistent-discount CEFs deliver a genuine
  **excess-of-cash return** (basket **+88 bps/mo, HAC *t* = +2.63**, bootstrap Sharpe CI
  **[0.12, 1.17]** clear of zero; PCEF +49 bps, *t* = +2.48), and their total returns clear cash —
  they are **not** the capital-destroying mirage of an mREIT. **But the claimed structural
  edge — discount pull + payout *beating the asset class* — does not clear the bar.** The
  excess-vs-excess Sharpe **trails SPY in every fund and every sub-era** (basket adv −0.21;
  −0.10 pre-2022, −0.36 post; PCEF −0.41), the CAPM alpha is ~0-to-negative (basket −1.6 %/yr
  *t* = −0.59; PCEF −3.3 %/yr *t* = −1.96), and β ≈ 1.0 (R² 0.73) exposes it as a **levered-beta
  income clone**. Real cash-plus return, no edge over the asset class → **Weak**. *Survivorship /
  ~11.5y history bias the magnitude upward — the honest read is if anything gentler.*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Costs are not the killer (net ≈ gross, +88.0 bps; ~15 bps spread on
  buy-and-hold turnover). What erases the proposition is a **hidden levered equity beta**: you get
  a better Sharpe holding SPY (0.82 vs 0.61), and in the 2022+ rate-hike regime the excess return
  collapsed to +32 bps (*t* = 0.62) with a −5.5 %/yr alpha and a −24 % drawdown year. A hidden
  beta erasing the edge is the textbook **Mirage**.
- **In one line:** the "discount pull *plus* payout" double-carry is half-true — the payout is a
  real excess-of-cash return, but the discount/asset-class *edge* is a levered-beta illusion that
  a plain SPY position beats on a risk-adjusted basis, and that the 2022 rate shock turned
  negative.
